label: Late-episode GO step after a rewarded a2 trial; silent after unrewarded or a1 trials.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * (ep_dec == 8) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * ((prev_reward == 0) | (prev_action == 1))
terms: (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * np.minimum(belief_lo, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_dec >= 7) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
explanation: Fires only at GO and only late in the episode (trials 70-99, which the timing baseline covers). Beyond timing, how large it gets depends on the previous trial: it is large after a rewarded a2 trial (largest after a2 S2 r, i.e. common-rewarded; smaller after a2 S1 r) and close to zero after any unrewarded trial or any a1 trial. So it acts like a late-episode signal to stay on a2 after a reward. D1 and D2 are always zero. The free fit adds the observer belief favouring S2 (graded, adds a little), a negative effect when the trial before last was rewarded, and splits the suppression into a1-rewarded vs unrewarded; this takes dev R^2 from 0.455 to 0.49. These scores are above the profile additive all ceiling (0.22) because the terms interact with the late-episode window. No future or model-output variables are used.

issues: The recorded short form reproduces (test R^2 beyond timing 0.467), but its a2 S1 r term adds almost nothing: dropping the third term, a2S2r + a2S1r scores 0.314 and a2S2r alone scores 0.312. Its weight is +0.05 against +0.25 for a2 S2 r, so the label's 'after a rewarded a2 trial' overstates the rare-rewarded case. The effect is essentially after a COMMON-rewarded a2 trial.

The third term ((prev_reward==0)|(prev_action==1)) adds 0.15 R^2, but mostly as a category split against the window-first '?' steps (prev_action unknown). With the per-decile baseline it amounts to an indicator for unknown-previous-trial. That is legitimate, but it is not a substantive 'drops after unrewarded/a1' effect beyond what the a2S2r indicator already gives. Misses still show systematic under-prediction at GO after '?' (+0.016).

The 'late episode' window is not uniform. The timing baseline peaks in decile 8 (0.197, against 0.075 and 0.087 in deciles 7 and 9), and the a2S2r boost scales with it. Adding (GO)*(ep_dec==8)*last_is('a2 S2 r') in place of the a2 S1 r term raises test R^2 to 0.523, above the claimed free fit of 0.503. Weights: +0.263 for decile 8 on top of +0.167 for deciles 7-9, and -0.122 otherwise.

With the improved form, misses leave only small residual classes: GO after '?' (+0.015) and GO after a2 S1 r (+0.014; some rare-rewarded a2 trials do fire strongly when belief still favours S2). There is no large systematic error. D1/D2 are correctly always zero.
The label's other claims check out: GO-only, silent after a1 trials whether rewarded or not (residuals all about -0.036), silent after unrewarded a2. No future or model-output variables are used.
